**Finding resubmitted: compliant — no redline.**

Summary of the repair: I kept the classification as compliant (the verifier confirmed this was the right call) and tightened the rationale to (a) cite p0025 alongside p0001 and p0023 as paragraphs checked and cleared, (b) state plainly that the absence of any audit obligation is better than the preferred position so no redline is warranted, (c) explain that the failed "audit frequency limited" check is non-probative because there is no audit clause for the frequency pattern to match, and (d) drop the out-of-scope aside about seeking audit rights against Kubient's "as measured by Kubient" reporting, which belongs to a Vendor-facing rule rather than this Customer-facing one.

Key points:
- No audit, inspection, records or verification right binds The Associated Press anywhere in the Agreement; searches for "audit", "inspect", "records" and "verif" all returned zero hits across the single-section document (p0000–p0074).
- p0001's "access, support and cooperation" is operational delivery cooperation, not an audit or system-access right; no provision grants direct or remote access to our systems, so there is no walk-away exposure.
- Since we face no audit obligation at all, we sit better than the preferred position, and flagging a deviation would risk inviting a right the Vendor never requested.
